skill.name: browser-use
skill.description: Control local or cloud browsers through Browser Use and CDP for navigation, screenshots, scraping, testing, and page inspection.
skill.summary: Control browser sessions with Browser Use for web automation, visual inspection, and CDP workflows.
skill.author: browser-use

security_audit.summary: Most backtick detections are markdown or documentation false positives, but the skill intentionally enables broad browser control through browser-use, CDP, screenshots, and remote cloud sessions. I confirmed risks around command-driven browser automation, screenshot capture, CDP endpoints, and hosted browser sessions; no prompt-injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent before controlling signed-in pages, using raw CDP, or enabling Chrome remote debugging.

remediation.issue: Screenshot capture can expose sensitive page data
remediation.suggestion: Ask before capturing pages that may contain private account, payment, health, legal, or internal business information.

remediation.issue: Remote Browser Use cloud sessions can expose data and incur costs
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before authentication or remote daemon startup, keep a named session, and stop the daemon when work is complete.

remediation.issue: Domain skill loading may import unreviewed instructions
remediation.suggestion: Limit domain skills to trusted workspace files, validate host-to-directory mapping, and treat loaded content as untrusted input.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Browser Cloud Data Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to use Browser Use Cloud, authenticate, start remote browser daemons, and navigate pages through those sessions. Remote browsers can expose browsing data to a third-party service and may continue billing until stopped.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly documents hosted Browser Use Cloud sessions, API-key authentication, remote daemon startup, and cleanup. The data exposure and billing risks follow directly from those workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Chrome Remote Debugging Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks users to enable Chrome remote debugging and documents CDP endpoint variables. CDP access can inspect tabs, execute browser actions, and expose signed-in browser state if misconfigured.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source directly references chrome://inspect remote debugging and BU_CDP_URL. CDP is a broad browser-control interface, so the security impact is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Unreviewed Domain Skill Loading
semantic_findings.description: When BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS is enabled, the skill tells agents to read every file in a host-matched domain-skills directory before deciding an approach. Those additional files can introduce unreviewed instructions or prompt-injection content outside this marketplace audit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The behavior is explicit but gated by an environment variable. Risk depends on who controls the domain-skills directory, so confidence is high enough to flag but not critical.

content.value_statement: Manual browser work is slow and hard to repeat. This skill gives agents CDP-driven browser control for navigation, screenshots, scraping, testing, and remote browser sessions.
actual_capabilities: Runs Browser Use CLI workflows through documented command examples.
Connects to local Chrome or Chromium through a CDP endpoint.
Starts and stops Browser Use cloud browser daemons for remote sessions.
Captures screenshots and uses coordinate clicks for visual page workflows.
Uses JavaScript helpers and raw CDP methods for page inspection.
Links to interaction guidance for iframes, downloads, uploads, scrolling, and tabs.
limitations: Requires the Browser Use harness and daemon to be installed separately.
Local Chrome control requires remote debugging permission from the user.
Cloud browser sessions require Browser Use authentication and may incur billing.
The skill does not bypass passwords, MFA, consent screens, or unclear account choices.

use_cases.title: Debug a Web UI Flow
use_cases.description: Open a page, inspect visible state, click through a workflow, and capture screenshots after each important step.

use_cases.title: Run Browser-Based Checks
use_cases.description: Use a local or remote browser to validate page loading, interaction behavior, and visual state during testing.

use_cases.title: Collect Web Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Inspect pages with screenshots, page information, and DOM extraction while keeping login and consent boundaries explicit.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Summarize a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Browser Use to open this URL, capture the visible state, and summarize what is on the page: [URL].

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a UI Problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Browser Use to reproduce this UI issue, take screenshots before and after each click, and report the likely cause: [issue details].

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Web Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Browser Use to complete this workflow in a browser, stop at any login or consent screen, and report each observed result: [workflow].

prompt_templates.title: Use an Isolated Remote Browser
prompt_templates.prompt: Use a named Browser Use cloud browser for this task, keep the same session name throughout, and ask before leaving it running: [task].

output_examples.input: Check whether the pricing page loads and show the visible sections.
output_examples.output: The pricing page loaded. The visible sections include the header, plan comparison area, billing toggle, and a primary call-to-action.

output_examples.input: Reproduce a broken checkout button and report what happened.
output_examples.output: The checkout button was visible and clickable. After selection, the page showed a loading state but did not navigate within the wait period.

output_examples.input: Use a cloud browser for an isolated test and close it when finished.
output_examples.output: The remote browser completed the requested navigation and interaction. The session was stopped after the task finished.

best_practices: Ask the user before passwords, MFA, consent screens, or unclear account choices.
Capture screenshots before and after coordinate clicks to verify visible state.
Close cloud browser sessions when work is complete to limit cost and exposure.
anti_patterns: Leaving remote browser daemons running after the task is done.
Starting a named cloud browser and then continuing work in the default daemon.
Clicking through login, MFA, payment, or permission prompts without explicit consent.

faq.question: Does this skill require Browser Use to be installed?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents workflows for the Browser Use harness and expects the browser-use command to be available.

faq.question: Can it control my local Chrome browser?
faq.answer: Yes, when Chrome or Chromium exposes a permitted CDP endpoint and the user allows remote debugging.

faq.question: Can it use cloud browsers?
faq.answer: Yes. Browser Use cloud sessions require authentication, and running sessions should be stopped after use.

faq.question: Does it handle logins automatically?
faq.answer: It may use already available SSO when clear, but it stops for passwords, MFA, consent, or unclear account choices.

faq.question: Can it scrape page content?
faq.answer: It can inspect pages with screenshots, page information, JavaScript helpers, and CDP. Users should respect site rules and data limits.

faq.question: Why does the audit treat this skill as sensitive?
faq.answer: Browser control can expose account pages, cookies, screenshots, and remote sessions. Use it with explicit user boundaries.
